title: Discovery: Migration from OpenAI to Dedicated - Lyric Labs
summary: Initial discovery: Lyric Labs currently uses OpenAI for prod inference, evaluating Redwood Dedicated for cost, latency and data residency. Key concerns: eval parity, model compatibility (vLLM/TGI), private VPC/KMS, SOC2/audit logs, and pilot benchmarking. Agreed next step: run a scoped POC with 2 models, share pricing and security pack, schedule SE deep dive for infra requirements.
action_items: Maya Liu: Send Dedicated sizing guide and preliminary pricing by 2026-09-16
Carlos Ortega: Share benchmark template + tokenization notes by 2026-09-17
Ravi Patel: Provide representative prompt set and traffic shape by 2026-09-20
next_steps: Redwood to share security pack (SOC2 report, encryption/KMS docs)
Schedule SE deep dive for infra (VPC/K8s/network) week of 2026-09-21
Start 2-week POC: run parity evals on chosen models (gpt-like & instruct)
transcript:
Header: 2026-09-14 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~42m
Attendees: Maya Liu (Redwood AE), Carlos Ortega (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (Lyric Head of ML), Sofia Nguyen (Eng Mgr), Tom Alvarez (Security), Aisha Khan (SRE)

Summary auto-gen: Lyric looking to reduce per-token cost, meet latency SLOs and keep data on dedicated infra. Interested in Dedicated offering and private deployment options.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, you should all be on mute unless speaking — i'm maya, i'll kick us off.
[00:18] Ravi (Lyric): hey thanks Maya, excited to chat — quick context: we run prod on OpenAI today, we have spikes up to 1200 rps, main issues are cost and some bursty latency.
[00:30] Maya: totally, and you mentioned you want some data residency and stronger control for models?
[00:36] Ravi: yeah, especially for some PHI-ish customer data, so we need dedicated infra or private deployment. also curious about eval parity — our outputs need to match current quality.
[00:50] Carlos (Redwood SE): hi all, i'm carlos; from an infra and model perspective, typical things we look at: model runtime (vLLM/TGI compat), tokenization differences, quantization and perf tradeoffs, and how your prompt sets behave.
[01:05] Sofia (Lyric): we do both chat-like assistant and instrutional completions; some models were fine-tuned. we're worried about compatibility for fine-tuned weights and any custom inference bits.
[01:17] Tom (Security): from security side, we need SOC2, SAML SSO, audit logs, and KMS integration for keys. also pan-eu data residency is a requirement.
[01:30] Maya: great, those are all supported patterns — Redwood Dedicated gives customer-isolated GPU pools, VPC peering, and KMS options. we'll share our security pack but just to call out, SOC2 and audit logs are standard for Dedicated.
[01:45] Ravi: can you run the same evals we run against OpenAI? we need parity on hallucination and few-shot performance.
[01:53] Carlos: yes, we typically do parity evals; two notes though: subtle tokenization differences can shift metrics, and if you use OpenAI-specific system prompts or finetune artifacts we might need conversion. we can run your prompt set and diff outputs, and tune model variants or temperature to match.
[02:12] Ravi: oh okay, is the conversion manual? we use a vLLM stack in-house for some internal tests and TGI for a few endpoints.
[02:20] Carlos: most of the time it's straightforward — vLLM/TGI runtimes are compatible but may require model re-quantization or kernel selection; and sometimes you see a tiny delta in deterministic outputs. we usually align tokens-per-second and run a param-sweep to get eval parity.
[02:38] Aisha (SRE): on networking, do you support private control plane or is it managed out of your VPC? we need the control plane to be on our infra for some customers.
[02:47] Maya: we offer a private deployment option where control plane sits in your VPC and ops plane is optional; for Dedicated we also do VPC peering and customer managed networking. we'll have Carlos follow up with exact requirements.
[03:02] Tom: what about encryption at rest and in transit? and KMS/HSM?
[03:07] Carlos: AES-256 at rest, TLS1.2+ in transit, and KMS integrations — we can integrate with customer KMS/HSM, export keys aren't needed. we'll include the crypto spec in the security pack.
[03:20] Sofia: curious about throughput — with our bursty pattern, what's the typical latency impact if we batch more aggressively to save cost?
[03:28] Carlos: batching reduces per-token CPU/GPU overhead but adds latency. Redwood runtime supports workload-aware batching: you can configure tail-latency SLOs and cost targets. in practice for chat workloads we tune batching by sequence length distribution; we can show you perf curves from similar customers.
[03:48] Ravi: are there customers who've migrated from OpenAI to Dedicated and kept the same eval numbers?
[03:55] Maya: yes, we've had a few; success depends on model selection and prompt-porting — often you run a small calibration POC.
[04:05] Ravi: calibration POC — what would that look like?
[04:09] Carlos: two-week POC: we ingest a representative prompt set, run parity evals on 1-2 model candidates (one gpt-like, one instruction-tuned), run throughput tests with your traffic shape, and produce a report with latency/cost tradeoffs.
[04:24] Aisha: what's needed from our side to start the POC?
[04:27] Carlos: sample prompts, sample payload sizes, tokenization artifacts if you have them, and access target dataset for evals — nothing heavy. and if you want private deploy we need networking details for scoping.
[04:40] Tom: on compliance, who has access to logs and KV cache? we need role-based access controls.
[04:46] Maya: RBAC is supported, audit logs are retained per your retention policy; KV cache is encrypted and access is limited to the customer's tenant keys in Dedicated.
[04:58] Ravi: budget question — roughly what's the cost delta vs OpenAI?
[05:03] Maya: it depends — for consistent high throughput Dedicated often becomes cheaper per-token. initial reserved capacity commitment required, but unit costs drop. we'll send a preliminary pricing model based on your 1200RPS burst and average token counts.
[05:20] Sofia: any gotchas migrating custom finetunes? we use OpenAI fine-tunes for some smaller models.
[05:27] Carlos: OpenAI fine-tune artifacts are not binary-compatible; we recommend re-exporting training data and redoing fine-tune in the target runtime or using a conversion path where applicable. we'll help scope that — sometimes replacement with an instruction-tuned base model plus a few-shot prompt works.
[05:43] Ravi: about vLLM/TGI — we've seen vLLM give faster latencies for long context. can Redwood match that?
[05:50] Carlos: our runtime implements similar KV cache and attention optimizations; depending on model architecture and quantization we hit comparable latencies. we can run a vLLM vs Redwood Dedicated head-to-head during the POC.
[06:07] Tom: legal/procurement: SCOT 2 — is there a DPA?
[06:11] Maya: yes, we have DPAs and can sign standard enterprise agreements. procurement will get the security pack and legal templates.
[06:18] Ravi: okay, let's talk technical constraints: we sometimes use sequence lengths up to 16k and memory spikes — can Dedicated handle that?
[06:27] Carlos: sequence length affects kernel selection and memory; Dedicated has options for larger GPU footprints and model sharding. we'll need to size GPU pools accordingly — share your distribution and we can propose config.
[06:39] Maya: also worth noting autoscaling and burst capacity options — you can reserve baseline and use burst for spikes.
[06:46] Aisha: monitoring — does Redwood expose per-request traces and token-level cost breakdown?
[06:52] Carlos: yes, Console gives token-level cost, per-model latency breakdowns, traces and retried error rates. we can grant access to a demo org for inspection.
[07:05] Sofia: any differences on embedding outputs if we switch models? our similarity indexes are sensitive.
[07:11] Carlos: embeddings vary by model and sometimes by tokenization; part of the POC is to run the same index build and measure retrieval metrics. if needed we'll recommend a model that matches your vector space properties.
[07:26] Ravi: what's the typical timeline from POC to production?
[07:30] Maya: typical is 4-8 weeks: 2-week POC, infra provisioning and secure onboarding ~1-2 weeks, then integration and rollout depending on your app.
[07:40] Tom: any support SLAs?
[07:43] Maya: Dedicated customers get higher SLAs and an assigned CSM; we can discuss SLA tiers.
[07:49] Ravi: ok sounds good. quick nit: sometimes internal folks call your product Redwood cloud, others call it Dedicated — will you provide doc mapping so we don't confuse teams?
[07:58] Maya: yes, we'll include a short one-pager on product modes and terminology.
[08:05] Carlos: for the POC, i'll need a sample of your fine-tuned artifacts if you want us to try porting, otherwise just prompts and traffic.
[08:14] Sofia: we'll put together a prompt dump and some eval labels.
[08:18] Ravi: last question — do you support Anthropic models or is it mostly OpenAI/model-catalog?
[08:24] Carlos: we support multiple open model families and can run Anthropic-like models if you have the weights; availability depends on licensing. the catalog includes curated variants.
[08:34] Maya: okay, let's recap next steps.
[08:37] Maya: action items: i'll send pricing + product one-pager; carlos will share benchmark template and security pack; ravi to send prompt set. we'll schedule SE deep dive for infra week of 9/21.
[08:50] Ravi: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[08:52] Tom: thanks, bye.

Notes: transcription has typical mislabels — sometimes 'vLLM' was transcribed as 'v-L-M' and 'TGI' as 'T-G-I'. There was minor crosstalk around 05:00-06:00 but content captured.
